doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Advice to young players
summary: Get out of the practice room and sit in at jam festivals; living in Rome, NY.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Well if you had any advice for guys who might be in college, those people who want to be where you are, what would you say to them? Don’t be taking my gigs?

Yeah. Just keep doing what you’re doing. Wow, get out as much as possible. Get out of the practice room, get out and play. Get over the hump of whatever, if you have stage fright or whatever, just try and find those situations and jump in. Like a lot of these what they call jam bands and jam festivals, go to festivals. Because a lot of it is open for people to sit in as well. A lot of these bands will see someone with a saxophone and will be like, “Come on” and you pretty much have opportunities to get out there and kind of explore and experiment with that scene you know. That would be my best advice, just to get out there and jump into it. That’s what I did.
Yeah. And living, I guess I asked this, but living in Rome, New York now, doesn’t make that much difference for the kind of gigs you play because you have to travel anyway.
Yeah. I mean I’ll get in the car to go to New York or Boston, it’s like a four hour trip or whatever. It hasn’t really changed, yeah, as far as what I need to get to.
